problem: Ellipsis checking discards every fragment shorter than 15 characters, including numbers, and then reports the remaining quote as verbatim. An invented or wrong numeric fragment can therefore pass the quote gate.
evidence: In-memory reproduction: found("This is a genuine long sentence ... 9999", norm("This is a genuine long sentence.")) returns True; quotecheck.py:19-22.
fix: Verify every quoted fragment, especially numbers, and distinguish an omitted fragment from a verified one.

problem: The checker verifies ellipsis fragments independently without checking order or span, so a quotation assembled in reverse order passes as verbatim.
evidence: In-memory reproduction: found("This is the second long sentence. ... This is the first long sentence.", norm("This is the first long sentence. This is the second long sentence.")) returns True.
fix: Match fragments in source order and retain enough location information to audit a stitched quotation.

problem: The table fallback accepts a value from the next species’ row as support for the current species, because it unions numbers from both lines. It also never checks which column contains the number.
evidence: In-memory reproduction: table_found("Felis catus 80", "Felis catus", ["Felis catus 20", "Canis lupus 80"]) returns True.
fix: Validate the actual row and column, using explicit wrapped-row handling; do not treat the next species’ values as interchangeable.

problem: Numeric normalization treats commas in CSV table rows as decimal/thousands separators, so correct CSV values are falsely reported absent. This produces false value-in-quote faults in existing evidence.
evidence: oa_lint.check(value=44, quote="104,44,18.7,60,126") reports "44 is not in the quote"; docs/views/evidence/oa-1.jsonl:408 is a real matching example.
fix: Parse table delimiters separately from decimal/thousands notation.

problem: The number matcher drops signs and scientific-notation semantics, so a value can pass even when the quoted sign is the opposite.
evidence: In-memory reproduction: check(value=-25, quote="25 degrees", otherwise populated source) returns no value-in-quote error; NUM matches digits without a sign.
fix: Compare parsed signed quantities, units, bounds and exponents rather than unsigned digit tokens.

problem: The quote-shape implementation rejects every lowercase ASCII opening even though its own documented rule exempts species epithets and units. Valid table/label excerpts can therefore fail the gate.
evidence: tools/views/oa_lint.py:10-11 explicitly exempts a species epithet or unit, but :57-58 implements only the lowercase test.
fix: Implement the stated exceptions and separate prose fragments from exact table labels.

problem: Any nonempty chased text and any two query strings count as a full search, including a statement that no citation step was run. The function also ignores the record’s date and whether the search failed.
evidence: searched_fully({"chased":"none: no step was run","queries":["one query","two query"]}) returns True; docs/views/research/THOROUGH.md:41-43 requires an actual citation/family step and says searches older than one year are redone.
fix: Represent protocol steps and outcomes explicitly, check distinct successful queries and expiry, and preserve incomplete searches as half-searched.

problem: Canon completion searches each entire evidence JSON line for DOI strings, so a DOI merely mentioned as a citation or unread lead can count as a compilation already logged. Retracted and failed stores are included too.
evidence: coverage.py:25-30 searches raw line text, rather than source.doi of accepted records; :45-50 then treats DOI membership as completion.
fix: Compute completion from actual accepted source records with the required trait/table coverage, using the same audited stores as the rest of the pipeline.

problem: Coverage matching does not require a negative finding to be a completed search of the named taxonomic level. It can also match a genus mentioned within a multi-name taxon string, and does not distinguish plant and animal homonyms.
evidence: coverage.py:81-91 matches text and protocol booleans without reading found/result, kingdom or an exact taxon ID.
fix: Use taxonomic IDs, explicit search scope and audited outcomes before marking a cell exhausted.

problem: The binomial parser turns uncertain identifications such as Uropeltis cf. macrolepis into the fictitious species key "Uropeltis cf". Uncertain, hybrid and multi-species names need separate handling.
evidence: In-memory parse_taxon("Uropeltis cf. macrolepis", "species", "", "", Tax()) returns species=["Uropeltis cf"]; canon-2.jsonl:104 uses this uncertain identification.
fix: Parse uncertainty markers without treating them as epithets and preserve uncertainty when deciding species-level evidence.

problem: Categorical disagreement compares only the first word, so opposite statements can be treated as agreement and synonymous descriptions as disagreement. This can both allow invalid carries and block valid ones.
evidence: In-memory disagree([m:"tapetum present", m:"tapetum absent"], "tapetum") is False, while horizontal slit versus horizontally elongated for pupil_shape is True.
fix: Normalize categorical states and compare the actual biological assertion; send unresolved conflicts for review.

problem: The gap builder reads raw evidence plus branch records, while rows and screening use audited corrected copies. Applied audit corrections other than retractions/partial flags are therefore not consistently represented in coverage.
evidence: gaps.py:150-159 reads docs/views/evidence; rows.py:101-113 substitutes docs/views/audit/corrected; gaps.py:146 accepts only partial fixes.
fix: Give gaps, rows, screening and canon completion one authoritative evidence loader.

problem: A grade-m string saying only that a source measured a trait closes a numeric cell, with no check that a usable measurement exists. This is already exercised by the appendix-only binocular records.
evidence: gaps.py:251-255 tests grade alone; docs/views/evidence/canon-3.jsonl:51-52,59,61-65 contain "visual field measured (type not stated in the appendix)" instead of a width.
fix: Distinguish an extracted measurement, qualitative evidence and a bibliographic lead before settling a numeric cell.

problem: Every existing record blocks a new search for a genus/trait, regardless of grade, missing value, eye, species or whether it is only a gene-based inference. This can prevent a search for the actual open measurement.
evidence: main_evidence at screen_candidates.py:110-123 applies no grade/value filter, and :183-184 fails every matching search; audit-74.md explicitly notes Zanda and Psephotus being held by inferred rows only.
fix: Compare evidence with the particular open cell and its required kind of measurement; show inferred/partial leads without treating them as definitive completion.

problem: The mechanical screening gate silently skips a genus absent from the harvest, so a record with no harvest provenance can pass with zero problems.

problem: The screening gate never checks whether the recorded queries match the harvest or whether a scientific/common-name web pair is present. An empty query list can pass if its candidate keys are populated.

evidence: screen_candidates.py:179-182 tests the wanted set only when the candidate is absent from screened.
fix: Record wanted/screened outcomes per work and trait, and fail unresolved contradictory outcomes.

problem: Harvest completion is checked only in harvest-cK files, so work finished by the desk under harvest-N/sweep units is scheduled again after the holds expire. All six batches now reopen despite nearly all their genera appearing in main’s search logs.
evidence: In-memory harvest_items(): batch genus counts 40,40,40,40,40,35; respectively 40,39,40,39,40,34 already appear in docs/views/searched; codex-gates.json holds expired on 26 October.
fix: Compute remaining traits globally per genus instead of inferring completion from the batch’s own filenames.

problem: OA completion is checked within each batch only, so a paper read in another batch can be offered again. This currently reoffers oa-11 entry 1 despite a full-read ledger elsewhere.
evidence: In-memory oa_items() compared with all accepted oa-*.jsonl read ledgers finds oa-11 entry 1 already read; codex_queue.py:55-60 considers only oa-11 and oa-none-11.
fix: Match completed full readings globally by source identity while preserving separate supplement/table scope.

problem: Distinct book chapters that share the whole-book DOI collapse into one wanted entry, discarding their separate titles/authors and permitting one reading to retire all of them.
evidence: docs/views/wanted/spider.jsonl:3,9-12,22 give different chapters under the same book DOI; wanted_csv.py:35-39 keys only by DOI.
fix: Give book/chapter requests separate identities and explicit scope; prefer verified chapter identifiers where available.

problem: When multiple wanted lines share a DOI, bibliographic metadata come from the first line and are never updated from later, more complete lines. Old placeholders can therefore beat registry-corrected entries.
evidence: wanted_csv.py:38-44 merges priority, units, views, targets and reasons but leaves authors/year/title/journal from the first record.
fix: Validate conflicting metadata and select verified fields explicitly rather than relying on input order.

problem: Explicit wanted-line traits are ignored: gain.py merges only taxa, rows and canon, then infers traits from row titles or prose. A precise traits list can be replaced by a broader heuristic match.
evidence: gain.py:58-61 ignores traits; :89-94 builds the filter from row titles and words, although wanted records carry traits fields.
fix: Merge and use explicit trait keys before any prose fallback.

problem: A valid empty wanted CSV crashes instead of producing an empty ranked list/status file.
evidence: gain.py:78 indexes data[0] unconditionally after csv.DictReader; an empty download queue is a normal terminal state.
fix: Use the input header and handle an empty row list explicitly.

problem: The refresh only creates unseen paper IDs and never updates metadata for papers already embedded or stored on the page. Corrected titles/authors/years in the repo do not reach existing page entries through this path.
evidence: papers_extra.py:14-15 excludes both BASE_IDS and HAVE_DIR IDs, while papers_refresh.py:38-40 updates status fields and only creates new extras.
fix: Produce versioned metadata updates for existing paper documents, with a defined process for embedded base records.

problem: The comparison tool’s docstring promises to report differing titles, but the implementation never compares the source title with the registry title. Wrong-work DOIs such as the owl entry can escape a title audit.
evidence: crossref_compare.py:1-4 says title differences are listed; the loop at :55-107 compares journal/authors/year only.
fix: Add an explicit title/identity check with appropriate handling of translations and book/chapter scope.

problem: The evidence validator accepts empty quotes and unusable values as long as required keys exist. It checks neither numeric types/units/bounds nor consistency between rank, taxon and trait.
evidence: check.py:25-53 checks key presence and quote length but not nonempty quote or value validity; the existing appendix-only measurements illustrate why this is material.
fix: Validate the meaningful value and quotation shape for each trait, while retaining an explicit schema for qualitative evidence.

problem: The append helper silently marks a record opened even when its author did not provide that attestation. This defeats the brief’s requirement that opened certify an actual reading.
evidence: addlog.py:33 supplies True before check.problems runs; BRIEF.md:62 requires opened only after reading the source in the session.
fix: Require an explicit opened value from the worker and reject an omitted attestation.

problem: Citation-step IDs from audited stores cannot be resolved because evidence_doi reads only docs/views/evidence/<unit>.jsonl. Units such as methods exist in audit/corrected, so their nearest-relative citation steps disappear.
evidence: ci/harvest/harvest.py:93-96 only opens the raw path; docs/views/audit/corrected/methods.jsonl exists while docs/views/evidence/methods.jsonl does not.
fix: Resolve a stable record ID through the same authoritative store used to produce closest_record.

problem: A genus is considered harvested successfully when its ordinary queries succeeded even if its citation chase or family-review step failed. The next ordinary run skips it, leaving a failed mandatory step unretried.
evidence: harvested_before at ci/harvest/harvest.py:322-323 checks only d.queries, although chase errors are separately written at :479-484.
fix: Track completion by required protocol step and retry failed chase/family steps.

problem: A newer failed genus harvest overwrites an older successful one; only family records have protection against this. The reviewer can lose a completed genus query set after a failed rerun.
evidence: harvest_get.py:40 overwrites genus unconditionally; :42-44 explicitly keeps an earlier successful family review.
fix: Merge successful genus steps or retain the latest successful result per query.

problem: Repairing a failed query in a supplement removes the failure only from extra queries, leaving the same failed original query in g.queries. The screening gate can continue rejecting the genus after a successful retry.
evidence: harvest_get.py:62-65 prunes x["queries"] for x in g["extra"] only; screen_candidates.py:169 checks failures in the original d.queries as well.
fix: Reconcile retries across original and supplemental steps, retaining the successful outcome and provenance.

problem: The OA step masks every nonzero script exit with || true, so a crashed lookup or encryption run can be reported as a successful job. A green job is not evidence that results were produced.
evidence: oa.yml:22 ends the complete python/tee pipeline with || true; the return step uses job.status.
fix: Preserve and report the script exit status while returning partial results in the always step.

problem: The oversize fallback deletes JSONL and compressed JSONL research results as if they were disposable binary files, although these are the principal outputs of harvest and Crossref jobs. It never rechecks that retained text is below the limit.
evidence: ci/return.sh:27-29 retains .txt/.json/.md/.csv/.log only; workflows return harvest.jsonl.gz and crossref.jsonl.gz.
fix: Preserve essential structured research results and choose a bounded return/archive strategy that explicitly reports any omitted artifacts.

problem: Copy failures while returning results are ignored, so the script can commit only metadata/index entries and still report that results were returned.
evidence: ci/return.sh:51 appends || true to cp and then commits/pushes without checking the expected output files.
fix: Fail or mark the return incomplete if copying required outputs fails; verify the destination before publishing.

problem: A failed plan command is followed by status=0; in plan-only mode the script exits successfully despite the failure.
evidence: The script has pipefail but no errexit, does not capture the plan pipeline status, and resets status immediately afterward.
fix: Capture and return the plan status before proceeding or publishing.

problem: A failed plan command is followed by status=0; in plan-only mode the script exits successfully despite the failure.
evidence: The script has pipefail but no errexit, does not capture the plan pipeline status, and resets status immediately afterward.
fix: Capture and return the plan status before proceeding or publishing.

problem: Draft publishing errors do not affect the workflow result because the script exits with the earlier model-run status. A successful model run with a failed push is reported as successful publication.
evidence: The put_branch.sh exit code is not captured; the final line is exit "$status", which was set from the Python run.
fix: Include publication failure in the returned status and keep partial results available for retry.

problem: Draft publishing errors do not affect the workflow result because the script exits with the earlier model-run status. A successful model run with a failed push is reported as successful publication.
evidence: The put_branch.sh exit code is not captured; the final line is exit "$status", which was set from the Python run.
fix: Include publication failure in the returned status and keep partial results available for retry.

problem: The whole-branch publisher does not validate its input directory or stop after a failed copy. It can create and force-push a branch containing only _made.txt when upstream output is missing.
evidence: put_branch.sh uses set -uo pipefail without -e, has no directory/expected-file check before cp, and later force-pushes unconditionally.
fix: Require the input directory and expected outputs, and stop if staging fails before committing or force-pushing.

problem: The OA worker prompt still limits m to one named species measured in that paper and caps all group values at g, contradicting the desk’s adopted rule for group statements and cited own-taxon measurements.
evidence: oa-pass.md:26 versus docs/views/audit/SAMPLE.md:47-51, "The rule decided"; QUEUE.md:194 records the later merged OA pass following the narrower desk rule.
fix: Make the active worker prompt and audit rule use one definition of m/g and partial.

problem: The outside-sweep prompt grades every agent-computed conversion i, while the brief permits measured quantities to be converted with arithmetic in note and current records are graded m for those same conversions.
evidence: external-sweep.md:24; BRIEF.md:60 evidence-log value rule; sweep-16.jsonl:2 gives an anatomical conversion at m with arithmetic.
fix: Specify how deterministic unit conversions, anatomical estimates and speculative predictions differ, and apply one rule consistently.

problem: The pass rule leaves an exactly 5% error rate undefined: this prompt says under 5% passes, whereas THOROUGH.md requires rechecking only above 5%.
evidence: desk-audit.md:9 (numbered step 5); docs/views/research/THOROUGH.md:68, "Three tests per burst", says "Above 5%".
fix: State the inclusive/exclusive threshold explicitly in all active prompts.

problem: A required audit-42.md reading is absent from main, and this prompt gives no branch/commit or alternate path to retrieve it. Auditors have had to recover it from an old commit by hand.
evidence: docs/tracks/progress/audit-42.md is absent; docs/tracks/progress/audit-67.md:190 says it had to be read at another commit.
fix: Provide a stable archived path or an explicit immutable reference for required reading.

problem: The gate note still describes harvest-c1..c6 as held for the desk, but their time-only holds have expired and the queue now reoffers them. The note does not capture current ownership/completion.
evidence: codex-gates.json hold timestamps are 2026-10-26T00:00:00+00:00; codex_queue.harvest_items currently reopens all 235 genera.
fix: Represent ongoing desk ownership and global trait completion explicitly rather than relying on an elapsed deadline.

problem: PDF and XML candidates are accepted even when title_in returns false: the identity rejection applies only to HTML. An unrelated PDF/XML can therefore be encrypted and labelled read despite failing the paper-title check.
evidence: oa.py:355-361 computes ok for every kind but continues only for a failed HTML match; its docstring promises to check that the text is the paper.
fix: Require a verified source identity for every format and retain failed identity checks as unresolved candidates.

problem: Semantic Scholar is queried only when earlier services advertise no candidates, so it is never tried when those advertised copies all fail to download or identify. Valid alternative copies can be missed.
evidence: oa.py:322-325 chooses S2 before fetching candidates; failure of all entries in the following loop has no S2 fallback.
fix: Try the remaining discovery service when no earlier candidate produces a verified readable copy.

problem: Metadata API errors are converted to None and lose their failure status; the final lookup can show no candidates without saying that discovery was blocked. A failed lookup is not evidence that no free copy exists.
evidence: jget at oa.py:60-66 discards status/error details; main records the service name in checked and receives no structured failure from it.
fix: Keep per-service HTTP/error outcomes and distinguish an unsuccessful lookup from a completed no-copy search.

problem: DataCite fallback is enabled only for a hand-supplied DOI list; the default sweep of evidence DOIs reports Crossref 404 for repository/dataset DOIs without trying their actual registry.
evidence: ci/crossref/crossref.py:70 gates datacite(d) on existence of ci/crossref/dois.txt, although the default evidence sweep includes dataset DOIs.
fix: Use registration-agency-appropriate lookup in both default and explicit-list modes, and distinguish non-Crossref registration from an invalid DOI.
